title: Steak and Mushroom Pie
subtitle: Slow-braised beef and chestnut mushrooms under puff pastry
excerpt: Tender chunks of braised beef shin with chestnut mushrooms in a dark, rich gravy, topped with golden puff pastry. The filling is made a day ahead; the pastry lid goes on at the last minute.

recipe.sourceNotes: Steak and kidney pie and steak and mushroom pie are the two great British beefsteak pies. The mushroom version omits kidney for those who find offal unwelcome, and the mushrooms provide the same earthy depth. The dish dates to at least the Victorian era and remains a British pub staple. Good beef shin is the traditional choice because its collagen dissolves into the gravy during the long braise.

content.text: Make the filling the day before and refrigerate it. Cold filling under the pastry is important: if the filling is hot when the pastry goes on, the fat in the pastry will melt before the pastry is in the oven, and the crust will be greasy and flat rather than flaky and puffed. Use a pie funnel or an upturned egg cup in the centre of the dish to support the pastry lid and prevent it sinking into the filling.
Toss the beef in seasoned flour. Heat the oil in a heavy pot over high heat and brown the beef well in batches, 4 to 5 minutes per batch. Remove and set aside.

Add the butter. Cook the onion over medium heat for 8 minutes. Add the garlic and mushrooms and cook for 5 minutes. Add the tomato puree for 1 minute. Pour in the Guinness, scrape the pan, then add the stock and Worcestershire sauce. Return the beef and add the herbs. Season.
Cover and braise on a very low heat for 2 to 2.5 hours until the beef is completely tender. Remove the bay leaves and thyme. Cool completely, then refrigerate overnight.

Heat the oven to 200 C / fan 180 C / gas 6. Spoon the cold filling into the pie dish. Cut the pastry to fit the top, with a 2 cm overhang. Press to seal, crimp the edges, and cut a steam hole in the centre. Brush with beaten egg. Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the pastry is deep golden. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.
